title: fix: Side chat blocks typing while answering
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Side chat disables its question box while answering, preventing users from drafting a follow-up.

## User Impact

Users can keep editing the next question during an answer. Sending still waits for the active answer; disconnected controls remain disabled. Drafts survive answer completion and errors.

## Why This Change Was Made

The textarea incorrectly shared the send button's busy guard. Keep its normal placeholder and let the existing thread status show that an answer is pending. Focus tests now wait for the pending exchange and explicitly establish the foreground input they intend to protect.

The failing cron recovery test compared process-wide work counts before and after an asynchronous operation. An unrelated root finishing changed 1 to 0 despite correct recovery. Recovery tests now borrow each timer's exact admission scope and verify it becomes unusable when that tick settles. This also detects a leaked tick even if unrelated work finishes. Startup, durable repair, events, reservations, and error-settlement assertions remain covered. Cron production code is unchanged.

## Evidence

- Final [hosted CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35672089372) and enforced merge gates passed for `d267c75cb0527f6d5ea4e8e908a58343b1713797`. The hosted cron cohort passed 1,562 tests across 126 files in 137.16 seconds; the three batch recovery cases took 975/24/24 ms. Merged as `368ec5c22d8cb1a3a5d106d305fee47eb3b08891`.
- Controlled before/after: releasing an independent request during held recovery makes the original assertion fail with the same expected-1/observed-0 result as [CI run 35655193743](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35655193743). The repaired three-file recovery suite passes all 36 tests (11.01 seconds wrapper wall).
- Mutation proof: temporarily omitting the timer's admission release makes both timer batch cases fail the new assertion; startup still passes. The mutation was removed before final validation.
- Full cron service cohort: 125 files, 1,557 tests passed with two workers (195.48 seconds Vitest). Side-chat component/history/lifecycle: 71 tests passed (5.83 seconds wrapper wall). Production-bundle Chromium focus suite: all 23 tests passed (30.87 seconds), including mobile, deferred mounting, pane switches, and newer input intent.
- Targeted type-aware lint and formatting passed. Changed-file checks passed repository guards and i18n, then stopped on unrelated configure/doctor types: this local install has Clack 1.5.1/1.8.1 from newer main while this head pins 1.5.0/1.8.0. Both core test-type shards passed on the exact head with frozen dependencies in [CI run 35672089372](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35672089372); those local errors do not reproduce there.
- Fresh independent autoreview found no P0 issues; the existing full side-chat review found no actionable issues through P2. The latest [ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/155183#issuecomment-5767395120) has no findings or rank-up moves.
- Production delta: +2/-2, net zero. Tests and support: +144/-21, net +123. No new production seam, reset, retry, timeout, or dependency change.
- The existing real-app screenshots below were inspected, verified to render in this PR, and delivered in the maintainer task. They use deterministic Gateway responses and the same 1440 × 900 viewport.

<details>
<summary>Investigation limits and follow-up</summary>

The original CI root's producer was not identified. Focused, predecessor-order, and complete shared-worker local runs did not reproduce that ambient root. The controlled concurrency scenario proves the count assertion is invalid; it does not claim an unidentified production leak was fixed.

Follow-up: inspect completion ownership in `src/cron/service/ops.run-admission-capacity.test.ts`, case "keeps saturated scheduled work unreserved when it is rescheduled". A diagnostic trace showed its immediate capacity recheck still open at file teardown; the case waits for listener removal rather than tick settlement. It ran after the failed recovery case in CI, so it cannot explain that failure.

Runtime deployment is separate; no hosting Gateway was restarted.

</details>
